name: Coral bleaching
summary: No new global bleaching event declared as of 15 Nov; scientists warn El Niño heat could bring one
state: Searches on 15 Nov found no declaration of a fifth global bleaching event and no confirmed regional mass bleaching. A global reef status report in September found reefs now get less time to recover between bleaching events as oceans heat up (Mongabay). GCRMN's Caribbean bulletin of 14 Aug, based on NOAA Coral Reef Watch, gave a greater than 70% chance of Alert Level 1 heat stress across most of the Caribbean by early November, so the level stays Normal with an upward trend.
for_you: Bleaching mainly affects reef-dependent fisheries, coastal tourism and shoreline protection in tropical countries. There is no direct effect on most readers.
rubric_hit: Normal: no global bleaching event in progress (none declared as of 15 Nov)

sources.title: Mongabay — Global coral reefs get less time to recover as oceans heat up, report finds

why: Reefs support a quarter of marine species and coastal economies; mass bleaching is a direct sign of ocean heat stress.
drivers: Marine heatwaves, El Niño, warming trend.
